prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 56-72 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a towering, menacing knight in heavy jagged dark gunmetal-grey plate armour (dark grey, not pure black), every plate edge and rivet lit in bright pale steel grey so each plate reads clearly, broad layered pauldrons with short hooked points, a closed dark great helm with two large curled ram horns of pale ash grey, and a wide T-shaped visor glowing bright ember orange-red from inside, the glowing visor large and clearly visible, a heavy broad two-handed greatsword with a notched edge held in both gauntlets, its blade upright in front of the body and its point well below the top of the grey box; a hunched, threatening stance; centred in its own cell with empty space on both sides; palette of dark gunmetal grey, bright pale steel grey, pale ash grey, dull bronze trim and bright ember orange-red. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: the closed great helm with pale ash-grey horns and the wide glowing ember orange-red T visor, the visor a clear bright spot.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, stepping forward toward the heroes at the end of a downward cut: the greatsword in both hands, its blade angled down in front of him with the point at knee height just ahead of his front foot, the whole sword well inside the middle cell (not raised overhead, not reaching the cell edge), the wide T visor glowing bright, facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, staggering, the horned helm tipped back with the glowing T visor still visible, the greatsword held upright across the chest in both hands, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. Use a clear diagonal line of action through the whole body, shift the weight onto one leg and lean the torso toward the heroes, the elbows bent, so the sword stays well inside its own cell. Draw only the parts named in the description, the same in every cell: no cape, cloak, tabard or extra cloth, and no slash trail, smear or motion lines. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, standing on two feet, both feet on the ground line. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, a cape, a cloak, a tabard, a shield, a skull, bones, a plume, gold armour, a second sword, a face, a crown, violet, purple, an all-black silhouette, pure black armour.
